Ruling: batch #311 item 1 · letter A · maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-10T07:10Z

Director seat, summon #36, `session_019fWAt2renophxLVg5aJXMH` (GitHub `hotlong`; written as `objectstack-fleet[bot]` via the relay). Batch #311 (three cards, this one first) was presented in chat with this seat's own readings and the recommendation A, fallback B; the maintainer answered 「同意」, which takes the recommendation. Freshness gate: the body (6,054 bytes, unedited since filing) and the comment list (none) were re-read before this record. Thread-read: none on this card.

## The ruling

- **A — the write authority over the security catalog stays what it is today.** After the cutover, positions, permission sets and capabilities are written through the metadata door only, and that door's gate stays `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict`: a system write, or a caller holding `manage_metadata` (the platform administrator, through `admin_full_access`). Organization administrators stay read-only on the catalog in every posture, as the anti-escalation rule in `default-permission-sets.ts` (lines 426–431 and 475–479 on `origin/main` `e22315238f`) has had it: letting them write would let an organization administrator bind `admin_full_access` to themselves. Setup's catalog pages show them the catalog read-only and say why.
- ⛔ **Not taken:** B (a new narrow "security catalog" system permission: a real enterprise pattern, zero measured pull, a permanent public surface, and still an escalation surface; it returns only with a named user) and C (opening the metadata door to organization administrators under `single`: a privilege-escalation path and a reversal of the anti-escalation rule, never a seat's to grant).

## Why A on the first axis

One rule: definitions belong to metadata authors, and the authority to author metadata is `manage_metadata`. A adds nothing and corrects a premise rather than a boundary. ADR-0131 D2's "the security-administration authority an organization admin holds today (the object grants on the catalog)" names an authority that, read against the code, is read-only, so A is the literal reading of D2, and D7's "for capability holders" is the accurate wording. B and C both widen; only B is ever admissible, and only on pull.

## Corrections this ruling makes

- This seat's own record 6094171670 on objectui#7611 (batch #310 item 1) said an organization administrator with no Studio capability creates and edits catalog items from Setup today and after the cutover, and named a "server half" (the metadata door accepting that administrator's write under `single`) as owed by the cutover. The premise was the ADR's sentence, not the code; the triage seat measured the code (this card), and the objectui lane already amended its copy (objectui#7611, 6094498192). The parity gate on objectui#7611 reads instead: under `single`, the platform administrator (a `manage_metadata` holder) creates, edits, deactivates and reactivates positions and permission sets from the same Setup page as today; an organization administrator sees the catalog read-only, with the reason. The "server half" item is withdrawn from the cutover plan (#15204).
- ADR-0131 D2 and D3 get one dated sentence in the §8/D14 execution-plan paragraph that #22619 owes (Tier H): the authority an organization administrator holds on the catalog today is read-only; Setup authoring under `single` requires `manage_metadata`; D7's "for capability holders" is the accurate wording. No decision of the record changes.

Prior rulings read: ADR-0131 D2/D3/D7; the anti-escalation rule (`default-permission-sets.ts:426-431`, `:475-479`); `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict` (`metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts:79-93`); `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` (`eval-user.zod.ts:141`, `manage_metadata`); S7's system-context definition write (`position-write-through.ts:112`); #22601 B (6094045326); batch #310 item 1 (6094171670); thread: none. 自检:只看①选 A;②③④是否翻转:否。

- This card closes `completed` in this act; `needs-user-decision` leaves with the close; `priority:p1`, `security`, `domain:services`, `target:v18`, `area:access` stay. The body gains its `Ruled:` line in the same act.
- Pointers: objectui#7611 (the parity gate as corrected above; the objectui lane builds it), #15204 (the cutover plan drops the server-half item; C7a's `--plan` on #22617 lists any custom permission set that grants a write on the four catalog objects), #22619 (the D2/D3 dated sentence). Workload of the chosen option, as the rule requires: zero server lines; C9's acceptance text rewritten.
